messages:
Maya Chen: FYI I'm getting a customer escalation — per-model throughput graphs for multiple models are showing flat zeros starting ~09:10 UTC. Customer says API QPS spiked but console shows 0. Can someone confirm?

Jordan Patel: I can see the same on the console for several routes. No alerts fired though. Is this after yesterday's metric change?

Maya Chen: Yes, we ran the metrics key rotation last night (metrics-service v2). Repro: go to Console -> Models -> Select model -> Throughput panel, time range last 6h. Panel shows constant 0.

Liam O'Neal: Can you paste the exact PromQL Grafana panel query? Might be a label mismatch.

Maya Chen: Panel query (old):
```
sum(rate(model_throughput[1m])) by (model)
```
But our metrics-exporter logs now emit `inference_runtime_throughput{model_id=...}` instead of `model_throughput{model=...}`.

Noah Rivera: Confirmed in prometheus: I see metrics with the new name `inference_runtime_throughput` and label `model_id`. The old metric `model_throughput` is gone after the relabel step. That explains the empty panels.

observability-bot: Prometheus scrape at 2026-03-17T09:11:02Z shows series: `inference_runtime_throughput{model_id="gpt-redwood-13b",region="us-west-2"}`. No series found for `model_throughput`. Link: https://prometheus.internal/query?g=... (redacted)

Jordan Patel: Ok. Short-term fix: update panels to accept either metric name/label so dashboards don't break during migrations. Example PromQL that works for both variants:
```
sum(rate(model_throughput[1m])) by (model) or
sum(rate(inference_runtime_throughput[1m])) by (model_id)
```
But Grafana needs consistent legend/label mapping. In the panel we can use: `label_replace` to normalize label name:
```
sum by (model_norm) (
  rate(model_throughput[1m])
)
or
sum by (model_norm) (
  label_replace(rate(inference_runtime_throughput[1m]), "model_norm", "$1", "model_id", "(.*)")
)
```
This will preserve old dashboards while we finish rollout.

Maya Chen: Thanks — can you push a quick dashboard patch? Customer is getting anxious.

Noah Rivera: I can push a hotfix for the Grafana dashboard (update queries) and also add a fallback recording rule in Prometheus to populate a `model_throughput` compatible metric via `record: model_throughput` using `inference_runtime_throughput` during the migration window. That'll keep alerts and dashboards stable.

Liam O'Neal: Longer-term: we should update our metrics migration playbook to include a dashboard compatibility step: create recording rules that map new metric -> old metric name for at least 24h, and update dashboards to tolerate both names. Also update the console migration checklist.

support-bot: Ticket #CS-4821 created: "Customer graphs showing zero QPS after metrics rename". Linked: internal runbook doc and affected customer.

Jordan Patel: Quick commands I used to test locally:
```
# query new metric
curl -g "http://prometheus/api/v1/query?query=sum(rate(inference_runtime_throughput[1m])) by (model_id)"
# query old metric (will return empty)
curl -g "http://prometheus/api/v1/query?query=sum(rate(model_throughput[1m])) by (model)"
```
Outputs show data only for the new metric.

Maya Chen: Customer updated: they can see live QPS via API logs, so service is fine. They'll hold until we patch dashboards. Thanks Noah/Jordan.

Noah Rivera: Patch pushed to Grafana provisioning (PR #3847). Also added temporary Prometheus recording rule: `model_throughput = sum(rate(inference_runtime_throughput[1m])) by (model_id)` with label rename. Alertmanager silenced for related alerts until dashboards are validated.

Liam O'Neal: I'll follow up to add the compatibility step to the migration playbook and run a smoke test next migration.

Maya Chen: Closing loop with customer now. Marking incident as support-escalation-resolved. :thumbsup:
